Magic and spell construction

The formulas below describe this engine's current rules. Item and spell examples are calculated from your loaded game data.

Spell damage

For a damaging spell, raw power starts at its calculated effect. If duration exceeds one tick, the tick factor is 4 / duration; both power and armor absorption are scaled by that factor. Matching natural armor and the strongest matching protection effect are subtracted first, then worn armor acts on each body part's share. The active armor rule sets the minimum damage.

Runes modify the prototype's effect, area, range, duration, targets or stamina cost. Changes of the same kind add relative to the prototype; they do not multiply one another. Each rune also adds its stamina cost, complexity and value.

Area radius = √(area / π). Stamina cost cannot fall below the prototype's cost. Duration modifiers add whole ticks. Filter and item-enchantment runes change targeting rather than power.

A character needs sufficient knowledge of the spell's school and sufficient maximum stamina to equip it. A legal rune also needs a compatible prototype and available rune slots.
